title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East (early show) on 1970-02-11
source: SBD MR > DAT (disc 1 and first part of Star, last part lovelight via a DAT transfer so is not from circ. source); MAR > ? > R @ 3 @ ips. (aud patch source used in Dark Star and Lovelight); SBD MR > A77 > A77@ 71/2 ips (primary source for disc 2); Transfer info:  Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre pair Tesla tubes circa 1980  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard composite of the early/late Fillmore shows, highlighted by a scorching Cold Rain jam and the Hammond‑driven Spanish Jam.
ai_review.review: The 126251.sbd.wolfe‑lee‑smith file is a well‑balanced soundboard composite that captures both the partial early set and the expansive late show. Reviewers rave about the Cold Rain improvisation, the first‑half brilliance of the Dark Star (mis‑typed “Dawk Staw”), and the Hammond‑fueled Spanish jam, while noting a few channel‑balance quirks on Uncle John’s and an unfocused Lovelight stretch.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed reviews give high marks (4–5★); musical performance is praised with several standout moments, and the soundboard source is regarded as one of the best composites despite minor channel issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and well‑balanced; some reviewers note a mono‑channel issue on Uncle John’s (one‑guitar mix) and occasional EQ/balance quirks in other sources, but this composite is considered the best available.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑show night with a fragmentary early set (Black Peter → Cryptical … Casey Jones) followed by an expansive late show featuring long jams, guest appearances and historic moments; the flow is praised for its historical significance even if not every jam lands.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar appears on the one‑guitar mix of Uncle John’s and contributes to the Dark Star instrumental section.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass work is highlighted in the Cold Rain jam and also part of the one‑guitar mix on Uncle John’s.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir (referred to as Bobby) shines in the Cold Rain improvisation.
